trigger: a crafted Mcp-Session-Id bisects a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence within its first 8 bytes
summary: substr(0,8) truncates before sanitize_detail_value runs, which can leave a bare UTF-8 continuation byte (untouched by the sanitizer, which only maps ';'/'='/control bytes) in the emitted prefix. classification_rationale: accurate, narrow, pre-existing observation

trigger: a crafted Mcp-Session-Id bisects a UTF-8 sequence in its first 8 bytes, orphaning a continuation byte in the sanitized prefix that reaches a Postgres-backed AuditStore INSERT
summary: Theorized that a truncation-orphaned UTF-8 continuation byte reaching Postgres could fail that row's own INSERT, an under-observed audit-persistence edge case. DISPROVEN by chaos-injector (Gate 5): AuditStore::log() passes every text column, including target_id, through sanitize_pg_text/sanitize_utf8_strict at the store layer UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of call-site behavior -- an existing mechanism (ADR-0040/#1593) built for exactly this class of hole. A bare continuation byte is replaced with U+FFFD, never fails the INSERT. Residual truth is only a display-fidelity nit (replacement char shown instead of the raw byte), not row loss.
classification_rationale: reasoned hypothesis, subsequently investigated and disproven with code evidence
adjudication_rationale: chaos-injector traced the full call chain (mcp_server.cpp -> try_persist_audit -> ServerImpl::audit_log -> AuditStore::log -> sanitize_pg_text) and confirmed no bypass exists; even counterfactually a Postgres INSERT failure would hit the SAME yuzu_server_audit_emit_failed_total counter as any other persist failure, not a distinct/less-visible path
